content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines scheduling and background-task concepts as part of email, background work, and external services. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Synchronous versus asynchronous work; Long-running operations; Queues, workers, and schedulers; Retries and idempotency; Choosing an external task system when needed. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Synchronous versus asynchronous work
items.text: Async code helps most when it can await non-blocking I/O; CPU-heavy work or blocking libraries can still stall the event loop. Test timeouts, cancellation, concurrency limits, and sync/async boundaries.
